Neon's docs say Scale to Zero suspends compute after inactivity, and that storage is billed on actual data size in GB-months, measured hourly, so storage is billed independently of compute state. The Neon pages do not explicitly say 'suspended databases still pay storage'; that follows from storage being billed on data size.
